title: From Qubit to Qubit: A Graduate Course in Quantum Mechanics
summary: This textbook is drawn from notes for a two-semester graduate course in quantum mechanics. It begins with the most constrained quantum system, and recovers the rest of the subject by relaxing those constraints one at a time. The starting point is a single qubit, the smallest nontrivial Hilbert space with the strongest possible restriction on its dynamics, made concrete by a Bloch cube whose six faces are the cardinal states of a spin-1/2 system. Tensor products admit many qubits; lattices give them a place to live; time evolution sets them in motion; the continuum limit produces…
